extDescription.message: Blocks time wasting sites and shows you a research fact instead. Take your time back.

insightsIntro.message: What research says about endless scrolling, and what happens when people cut back. Every fact links to the original study.

insightText1.message: Just having your phone within reach drains brainpower. In two experiments, its mere presence reduced people's available cognitive capacity, most of all for the most phone dependent.

insightSource1.message: Ward et al. (2017), Journal of the Association for Consumer Research

insightText2.message: Short video feeds make you forget what you meant to do. In a 2023 experiment, only the TikTok style feed hurt people's memory for planned tasks; Twitter and YouTube did not.

insightSource2.message: Chiossi et al. (2023), CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems

insightText3.message: Students who limited Facebook, Instagram and Snapchat to 10 minutes per app per day for three weeks felt significantly less lonely and less depressed.

insightSource3.message: Hunt et al. (2018), Journal of Social and Clinical Psychology

insightText4.message: People who deactivated Facebook for four weeks spent more time with friends and family, reported higher well being, and used it less even after the experiment ended.

insightSource4.message: Allcott et al. (2020), American Economic Review

insightText5.message: A one week break from Facebook raised life satisfaction and positive emotions among 1,095 people, with the biggest gains for heavy and passive users.

insightSource5.message: Tromholt (2016), Cyberpsychology, Behavior, and Social Networking

insightText6.message: Young adults in the top quarter of social media use had about twice the odds of sleep problems compared with the lightest users, in a survey of 1,788 people.

insightText7.message: Researchers who developed a scale for doomscrolling found it linked to anxiety, poor self control, fear of missing out and problematic social media use.

insightSource7.message: Sharma et al. (2022), Technology, Mind, and Behavior
